title: print()
summary: Write objects to a text stream, separated by `sep` and followed by `end`.
description: Converts each argument with `str()` and writes the result. Returns None — it is called for its side effect, so it can never be part of an expression that needs a value.

parameters.name: *objects
parameters.description: Values to write; each is converted with str().

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Destination stream; use sys.stderr for error output.

parameters.name: flush
parameters.description: Force the stream to flush immediately.

real_world_usage: Fine for scripts and debugging. In anything that runs unattended, use the `logging` module instead: print has no level, no timestamp and cannot be turned down in production.

common_mistakes.fix: print returns None. It writes; it does not produce a value.
Use logging — you get levels, timestamps, and runtime configuration.

performance_notes: Each call may flush, which is a syscall. Printing inside a tight loop can dominate runtime; build the output and print once.
security_notes: Never print secrets. Standard output is frequently captured and retained by CI systems, container runtimes and log aggregators.
